Full Post Content:
We have completed 5,000+ professional dog walks across 21 areas in Mumbai.

Not casual strolls. Every walk is GPS-tracked, timed, and followed by a detailed report to the pet parent.

Building this taught me 3 things about hyperlocal marketplaces that most founders learn too late:

1. Supply quality is more important than demand generation.

You can spend lakhs on ads. But if the person walking the dog shows up late or cannot handle a reactive dog, you have lost that customer forever. We spend 3x more on Guardian training than on marketing. That is by design.

2. Density wins, not coverage.

We could have launched in 5 cities. Instead, we went deep in Mumbai. 21 areas, backup Guardian coverage, fast response times. Hyperlocal does not work if you are spread thin.

3. Trust is a system, not a feeling.

Pet parents do not trust you because you say trust us. They trust you because they see the GPS route in real time, get photos mid-walk, and know their Guardian is certified and insured. We engineered trust into every touchpoint.

Building Platypus is an operations problem wrapped in a technology problem. That is exactly the kind of problem I love solving.

6:00 AM - A Guardian calls in sick. I need a backup in place for 4 dogs across Bandra before 7 AM.

9:00 AM - GPS shows a Guardian deviated from the usual route. Check in. Construction on the regular path. Update routes for all Guardians in that area.

11:00 AM - New Guardian application comes in. Review credentials, schedule interview, plan training timeline.

2:00 PM - Monthly data review. Which areas need more coverage? Where is retention dropping? Which Guardians are consistently rated highest?

4:00 PM - Pet parent wants to upgrade from once-daily to twice-daily walks. Coordinate evening Guardian coverage for their area and breed.

6:00 PM - Evening walks begin across 15 areas. Monitor all GPS tracks.

8:00 PM - Review post-walk reports. Flag health observations to pet parents who need to know.

This is logistics, HR, operations, product development, and customer service running simultaneously, every single day.

Dog walking is not simple. Building a reliable, trustworthy, scalable dog walking service is one of the most complex operational challenges I have ever worked on.

And I would not trade it for anything else.
